arxiv-1404-7458.title: Automata in SageMath—Combinatorics meets Theoretical Computer Science
arxiv-1404-7458.creator: Clemens Heuberger, Daniel Krenn, Sara Kropf
arxiv-1404-7458.description: Abstract The new finite state machine package in the mathematics software system SageMath is presented and illustrated by many examples. Several combinatorial problems, in particular digit problems, are introduced, modeled by automata and transducers and solved using SageMath . In particular, we compute the asymptotic Hamming weight of a non-adjacent-form-like digit expansion, which was not known before.

arxiv-2107-05051.title: On the Expressiveness of Assignment Messages Journal: Economic Letters
arxiv-2107-05051.creator: Maximilian Fichtl, Technical University of Munich
arxiv-2107-05051.description: Abstract In this note we prove that the class of valuation functions representable via integral assignment messages is a proper subset of strong substitutes valuations. Thus, there are strong substitutes valuations not expressible via assignment messages. 1 Introduction Strong substitutes valuations are an important class of valuation functions for indivisible markets, guaranteeing existence of a Walrasian equilibrium.

arxiv-2201-00620.title: Overview of the EEG Pilot Subtask at MediaEval 2021: Predicting Media Memorability Conference: Multimedia Evaluation Workshop; December 13-15 2021; Online
arxiv-2201-00620.creator: Lorin Sweeney 1 , Ana Matran-Fernandez 2 , Sebastian Halder 2 , Alba G. Seco de Herrera 2 , Alan Smeaton 1 , Graham Healy 1
arxiv-2201-00620.description: Abstract . The aim of the Memorability-EEG pilot subtask at MediaEval’2021 is to promote interest in the use of neural signals—either alone or in combination with other data sources—in the context of predicting video memorability by highlighting the utility of EEG data.

arxiv-2308-10045.title: An Empirical Study of CLIP for Text-based Person Search
arxiv-2308-10045.creator: Min Cao, Yang Bai, Ziyin Zeng, Mang Ye, Min Zhang
arxiv-2308-10045.description: Abstract Text-based Person Search (TBPS) aims to retrieve the person images using natural language descriptions. Recently, Contrastive Language Image Pretraining (CLIP), a universal large cross-modal vision-language pre-training model, has remarkably performed over various cross-modal downstream tasks due to its powerful cross-modal semantic learning capacity.

arxiv-2312-00153.title: Dynamic Phase Transition in 2D Ising Systems: Effect of Anisotropy and Defects
arxiv-2312-00153.creator: Federico Ettori, Thibaud Coupé, Timothy J. Sluckin, Ezio Puppin, Paolo Biscari
arxiv-2312-00153.description: Abstract We investigate the dynamic phase transition in two-dimensional Ising models whose equilibrium characteristics are influenced by either anisotropic interactions or quenched defects. The presence of anisotropy reduces the dynamical critical temperature, leading to the expected result that the critical temperature approaches zero in the full-anisotropy limit.

arxiv-2312-07035.title: HyperRouter: Towards Efficient Training and Inference of Sparse Mixture of Experts
arxiv-2312-07035.creator: Giang Do, Khiem Le, Quang Pham, TrungTin Nguyen, Thanh-Nam Doan, Binh T. Nguyen, Chenghao Liu, Savitha Ramasamy, Xiaoli Li, Steven Hoi
arxiv-2312-07035.description: Abstract By routing input tokens to only a few split experts, Sparse Mixture-of-Experts has enabled efficient training of large language models. Recent findings suggest that fixing the routers can achieve competitive performance by alleviating the collapsing problem, where all experts eventually learn similar representations.

arxiv-2406-10602.title: Multilingual Large Language Models and Curse of Multilinguality
arxiv-2406-10602.creator: Daniil Gurgurov, Tanja Bäumel, Tatiana Anikina
arxiv-2406-10602.description: Abstract Multilingual Large Language Models (LLMs) have gained large popularity among Natural Language Processing (NLP) researchers and practitioners. These models, trained on huge datasets, show proficiency across various languages and demonstrate effectiveness in numerous downstream tasks. This paper navigates the landscape of multilingual LLMs, providing an introductory overview of their technical aspects.

arxiv-2408-13375.title: Yang-Baxter extremal characters of wreath products of finite groups with the infinite symmetric group
arxiv-2408-13375.creator: Hicham Assakaf
arxiv-2408-13375.description: Abstract Let T T be a finite group. To a representation π \pi of T T and an involutive solution of the Yang-Baxter equation (an R R -matrix) verifying the "extended" reflection equation , we associate a character of a representation of the wreath product G := T ≀ 𝔖 ∞ G:=T\wr\mathfrak{S}_{\infty} .

arxiv-2408-16013.title: On the practicalities of producing a nuclear weapon using high-assay low-enriched uranium
arxiv-2408-16013.creator: P. Cosgrove, N. Read
arxiv-2408-16013.description: Abstract It was recently argued by Kemp et al. that HALEU (high-assay low-enriched uranium, or uranium enriched up to 19.75%) can conceivably be used to produce a nuclear weapon and on this basis civilian enrichment limits should be lowered to 10% or 12% [ 1 ] . We find their argument unconvincing in several respects.

arxiv-2410-20929.title: Two-spinon effects on the thermal Tonks-Girardeau gas
arxiv-2410-20929.creator: Felipe Taha Sant’Ana, Hui Liu
arxiv-2410-20929.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Felipe Taha Sant’Ana, Hui Liu. We study the effects of the two-spinon excitations on the field-field correlator of the Tonks-Girardeau gas. While these excitations have been previously examined in the ground state of the system, their role at finite temperatures remains unexplored. Here, we extend the analysis to the one-dimensional interacting Bose gas at thermal equilibrium, focusing on the one-body correlation function of the infinitely repulsive Lieb-Liniger model.

arxiv-2504-10238.title: Highly Hydrogenated Monolayer Graphene with Wide Band Gap Opening
arxiv-2504-10238.creator: Alice Apponi 1,2, Orlando Castellano 1,2, Daniele Paoloni 1,2, Domenica Convertino 3, Neeraj Mishra 3, Camilla Coletti 3,4, Carlo Mariani 5,6, Alessandro Ruocco 1,2
arxiv-2504-10238.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Alice Apponi 1,2, Orlando Castellano 1,2, Daniele Paoloni 1,2, Domenica Convertino 3, Neeraj Mishra 3, Camilla Coletti 3,4, Carlo Mariani 5,6, Alessandro Ruocco 1,2. arxiv-2505-21114.title: Differentiable Solver Search for Fast Diffusion Sampling
arxiv-2505-21114.creator: Shuai Wang, Zexian Li, Qipeng Zhang, Tianhui Song, Xubin Li, Tiezheng Ge, Bo Zheng, Limin Wang
arxiv-2505-21114.description: Abstract Diffusion models have demonstrated remarkable generation quality, but at the cost of numerous function evaluations. Advanced ODE-based solvers have recently been developed to mitigate the substantial computational demands of reverse-diffusion solving under limited sampling steps. However, these solvers, heavily inspired by Adams-like multistep methods, rely solely on t-related Lagrange interpolation.

arxiv-2509-11922.title: BuildingGym: An open-source toolbox for AI-based building energy management using reinforcement learning
arxiv-2509-11922.creator: Xilei Dai, Ruotian Chen, Songze Guan, Wen-Tai Li, Chau Yuen
arxiv-2509-11922.description: Abstract Reinforcement learning (RL) has proven effective for AI-based building energy management. However, there is a lack of flexible framework to implement RL across various control problems in building energy management. To address this gap, we propose BuildingGym, an open-source tool designed as a research-friendly and flexible framework for training RL control strategies for common challenges in building energy management.

arxiv-2511-14823.title: Dynamic Nested Hierarchies: Pioneering Self-Evolution in Machine Learning Architectures for Lifelong Intelligence
arxiv-2511-14823.creator: Akbar Anbar Jafari, Cagri Ozcinar, Gholamreza Anbarjafari
arxiv-2511-14823.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Akbar Anbar Jafari, Cagri Ozcinar, Gholamreza Anbarjafari. Contemporary machine learning models, including large language models, exhibit remarkable capabilities in static tasks yet falter in non-stationary environments due to rigid architectures that hinder continual adaptation and lifelong learning. Building upon the nested learning paradigm, which decomposes models into multi-level optimization problems with fixed update frequencies, this work proposes dynamic nested hierarchies as the next evolutionary step in advancing artificial intelligence and machine learning.

pmc-11654184.description: BackgroundThe implementation of early essential newborn care (EENC) is important to maternal and neonatal health. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the effects of EENC during and after cesarean section.MethodsA randomized controlled trial was conducted at a tertiary hospital in Wuhan, China.

pmc-12431441.title: Wearable SIMO Inductive Resonant Link for Posture Monitoring
pmc-12431441.creator: Giuseppina Monti, Daniele Lezzi, Luciano Tarricone, Ewa Korzeniewska
pmc-12431441.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This paper explores the feasibility of using a wireless Inductive Resonant Link (IRL) for wearable posture monitoring. The proposed system is based on magnetically coupled textile resonators and is implemented using a Single Input Multiple Output (SIMO) configuration. In particular, the setup consists of four inductively coupled resonators: one transmitting coil integrated into a textile structure and positioned on the back of the neck, and three receiving coils placed on the shoulders.
